_what_this_is: cascadia unsegmented, on PTHA18's own per-unit-source statistics table. Every rate parameter is read from an official file or derived by an official rule; none is typed by hand. Generated by official_ptha_data/fetch_official_inputs.py - re-run that rather than editing this.
_geometry_provenance: OFFICIAL, verbatim. unit_source_statistics_cascadia.nc from NCI THREDDS SOURCE_ZONES/cascadia/TSUNAMI_EVENTS/. Summing length*width reproduces the session's sourcepar$area = 169257.5245 km2 and the angle-averaged dip reproduces sourcepar$mean_dip = 10.1246780 deg, both to machine precision. That is what confirms it is the geometry the official rates were computed on. The mesh cannot be rebuilt from parameters: PTHA18's contour and down-dip inputs are unpublished and were hand-edited.
_convergence_provenance: RECOVERED from the saved session by inverting compute_rates_all_sources.R line 432: convergence = sourcepar$slip (0.0382820407134246) * 1000 * sourcepar$cos_dip (0.984427556139123). This zone has use_bird_convergence=1, so its convergence is an area-weighted average of unpublished per-unit-source Bird (2003) vectors and cannot be read from any file. The inversion is validated on puysegur2, where it returns 35.0000000000 against a CSV value of 35.
_coupling_provenance: READ from the sourcezone_parameters.csv row for cascadia: cmin/cpref/cmax = 0.7/0.8/0.9. Do not substitute the report's generic [0.3, 0.5, 0.7] triple from Section 3.7.2.3; on puysegur2 that cost -12.7% on the mean slip rate while leaving the slip-rate axis itself exact.
_mw_max_anchor_provenance: DERIVED, never typed. The literal string 'derive' makes the runner apply the rule in compute_rates_all_sources.R (lines ~293-363): lower = max(mw_max_observed + 0.05, 7.35); upper = min(Strasser area bound at -1 SD, Strasser width bound at -2 SD). The upper anchor is deliberately NOT capped here - the driver interpolates the 40 slots first and applies pmin(..., 9.6) afterwards, under its own comment 'Clip AFTER interpolation' (line 358). Doing it in the other order changes which values the axis holds on any zone whose raw anchor exceeds 9.6 (by -0.57% to -1.12% on the weighted mean Mw_max).
_moment_below_mwmin_provenance: TRUE, matching compute_rates_all_sources.R line 634. It controls how much seismic moment the balance attributes to earthquakes below Mw_min, so it moves the derived 'a' in a way that depends on b and Mw_max but not on slip_rate.
_observed_seismicity_provenance: OFFICIAL, read from the saved PTHA18 session, not re-derived from a catalogue. compute_rates_all_sources.R passes the GCMT subset to rate_of_earthquakes_greater_than_Mw_function as Mw_count_duration and Mw_obs_data (line ~631), so both live in the closure of the stored mw_rate_function and come back out by reading its environment. This zone carries 1 event(s) above Mw 7.15 in 41.1636 years, with the individual magnitudes listed. Because these are the very numbers the published posterior was computed from, the LEVEL 3 update reproduces the official result exactly rather than plausibly - which re-running the catalogue selection of gcmt_subsetter.R (buffer 0.4 deg, rake and strike within 50 deg, depth <= 71 km) could not guarantee on its own. The duration is the GCMT window 1976-01-01 to 2017-03-01.
_bird_model: Added by step8_official.py: per-column Bird (2003) profiles on the official mesh (lib/bird_convergence.py). Their area-weighted mean reproduces the official convergence to 1.9e-16 (relative).
